data.name: 5089: The Action RPG
data.detailed_description:
WARNING: This game is deep & complex! Take a moment to look over the Quick Guide: Watch the SteamVR mechanics video if playing in VR. 3089 vs 5089 questions? FAQ here.

5089 expands upon 3089, bringing you back to planet Xax 2000 years later. After the mysterious events in the year 4089, the Overlord hasn't been heard from for the last millennium, and so the experimental robots have continued to wage war according to their program. Without the Overlord to repair the damage, Xax has fallen into a state of chaos and dereliction. However, a shadowy new power has risen... how will your presence turn its fate?

Shoot, sneak, build, talk, slash, buy, sell, fly, swing, hover, scavenge, teleport & conquer your way through an endlessly generated planet. You can do it all with a friend, too. 5089 includes a rework of 3089 & does not require the original to play.

Newly Added & Key Features

  • Virtual Reality: Play 5089 with any SteamVR device, like the Rift or Vive! Want to sit, stand or use your whole room with tracked controllers? Go for it! Make sure to watch the SteamVR mechanics video alongside the trailer! (See forum for more VR details)
  • Dialog System: 5089 doesn't just have a new story, it has a new way to interact with it. You'll be talking with your fellow robots & more, and what choices you make will have consequences...
  • New Content: New robot types, new buildings, a new automatic weapon, a new gravity utility, new quest types, enemy shield system, item part color customization, story tidbits...
  • Improved Visuals: Better textures, new shaders, redone lighting system, improved animations, additional models... everything should just look more polished & better.
  • New Conversion Mechanic: Planet Xax is crumbling; you'll need to reclaim & destroy the enemy to improve the infrastructure!
  • Item Comparisons: Hover one item over another to see stats for both, or see how a part will integrate with another...
  • All New Original Soundtrack: Music specifically crafted for 5089 by Sorath72.
  • Easier Learning Curve: Game mechanics are introduced better, improved in-game tips, restructured heads-up display with better labels, added item usage instructions to the inventory & item parts are outlined to make item customization easier.
  • Over 130 Robot Quotes: Many from fan suggestions!
  • Balancing Overhaul: Economy has been revamped, item stats changed, difficulty curved tweaked, aiming system improved...
  • Better Performance: Even though 5089 is more detailed, engine reworks shall allow 5089 to run faster than its predecessors!
  • Advanced Terrain Generation: Buildings will now be placed in flatter areas, roads will be smoother...
  • 2-Player Co-op: 5089 now uses UPnP to automatically configure your router to forward ports if needed. Also, when Steam is run as administrator (and as a result, 5089 too) on Windows, it will automatically update Windows Firewall to allow communication. These improvements should make co-op play easier to setup!
  • Unlockable Classes: Beat the game to unlock 2 new starting classes!
  • Steam Integration: Achievements & Cloud game saves!

5089 uses Java 8 & 64-bit runtimes are included. If you have trouble running or questions about 5089, please post in the forum!

Trailer music by Pr0Beats, "Injustice"

data.short_description: 5089 is a deep & complex action RPG featuring strong sandbox roots. VR is supported, but not required. Watch the tutorial & VR videos next to the trailer! Everything is procedurally generated, like terrain, enemies, weapons, items & quests. Planet Xax's war rages on... how is that possible?

reviews.review:
About 300 reviews, 80% positive, and 5 years of updates: I was ready for a janky but interesting indie, but this is so bad it's hard to explain, not only is every single system is conceptually unsound and executed poorly but they all combine into something worse than the sum of its flaws.
Let's try to give you an idea by looking at how inventory/weight limits, player stats, death, and saves work together.

In this game, you have autosaves only and a single save slot per character, so if you end up in a bad situation you can't roll back to an earlier save.
Also, when you die you will lose a single item in your inventory: if that item is a random weapon part you picked up as loot it's not terrible, if instead you lost a component of some equipment (such as a weapon or a piece of armor) that equipment stops working and won't be back online until you slot in another component in the empty slot, the replacement also has to be in a fairly narrow level range compared to the components still there or you'll get a massive penality.
Sounds annoying but easy to work around, right? Just carry or stash spare weapons and armor so you'll never be left unable to recover, right?
You don't have a stash, your inventory slots are very limited (in no small part due to inane mechanical limitations such as needing a free slot if you want to use a hoverboard, because enabling/disabling the hoverboard without equipping/unequipping it from its slot was clearly beyond the dev's meager coding skills), and even worse your carry weight limit is so absurdly low you'll struggle to carry a full suite of armor and 2 weapons without significant investments into Agility.
Ok, let's raise Agility then, that means grinding skill points from super bland proc-gen quests (while avoiding the majority that generate with mandatory stealth objectives, since those require big investments into Stealth to be even theoretically possible), surely once you get a decent amount of Agility you'll be set for the whole game, right?
Higher level equipment weights more, and it's such a steep increase you soon won't be able to jump at all unless you keep pumping the majority of your skill points into Agility: and if you think of sticking to lower level equipment, equipment stats get so much better with level you'd be even worse off even if you put all your skill points into the relevant damage stat to compensate.
Notice I said "damage stat", increasing your Melee or Guns skill doesn't let you use those weapons better (such as swinging faster or reducing your spread as you keep shooting), it just increases a damage multiplier.
The weapons themselves aren't any better, you'd expect procgen to be a great way to get a fun and varied arsenal but there's only 4 actually distinct weapon types that get then multiplied by more inane mechanical limitations such as "Rifle" and "Energy Rifle" needing to be distinct weapon types instead of the ammo type being a modifier of one of the weapon parts (that's how bad the dev is at coding), also part stats are calculated out of a budget that depends on a part's level so all you get to do is roll for the few combinations of basic tradeoffs that don't completely suck.

That's the bulk of the gameplay by the way, you safely grind easy and meaningless "content" (generous usage of the word) to pay a truckload of skill/credit taxes so you can make your damage numbers bigger so you can safely and easily grind equally meaningless "content" with an higher level number attached to it, and occasionally enjoy being set back a few hours when you die to some nonsense such as the vehicle you're in grazing a two pixels wide floating triangle of procgen terrain.

After slightly more than 2 hours of playing I had barely made it to level 3 equipment and defeated the first "boss" (again, generous usage of the word, just a normal enemy but scaled up to the point its movement code barely works and  also given an obscene amount of health + regenerating shield), and to see if there was anything worthwile somewhere behind all that grind I hacked the game to multiply skill/credit gains by 10.
There is, in fact, a bit of stuff that's not immediately visible and only noticeable after what should equate to a dozen to a hundred hours of legit grind: there's new movement options such as teleporters and grappling hooks (very cool, but they're still equipments so good luck getting enough Agility to carry them too), there's vehicles (great way to travel quickly, also great at fighting if they happen to spawn with weapons, you need massive investments in Piloting or you'll be simply locked out of using them, yes the Piloting requirements will scale just as badly as the Agility requirements mentioned above), there's building mechanics (you can spend hours setting up teleporter networks so you can revisit those low level areas that no longer have anything to offer you, yay), there's even a whole THREE new enemy types (out of maybe 10) that only appear if you progress the main quest far enough!
If you've read other reviews you might have seen complaints about how you can lock yourself out of the main quest by picking the wrong dialog choices, not only I can confirm that but I'm pretty sure that you can also lock yourself out of two of those three new enemy types if you lock yourself out of the main quest at the wrong time.

Some misc observations to conclude:
[list]
    [*]The bosses after the first are just the first boss again, but with bigger stats and further away from your position to waste your time.
    [*]Escort quest are best completed not by attempting to actually escort the bot you're supposed to protect (and blowing a gasket as it fails to pathfind and humps a wall instead of taking the stairs 2 cm to the side because, once again, the dev can't code worth a damn), but by running ahead to the destination, the bot will just teleport to you every couple seconds and thus negate the whole point of the quest. 
    [*]If you manage to go out to areas level 10-15 (don't even attempt without cheats) you can see some variety in the terrain procgen, revealing you're on an island connected to other islands by enormous land bridges: it's the first and only cool terrain gen I've seen, it's also terrible for gameplay because out there objectives will often spawn underwater and that makes things even slower.
    [*]Once you cut out all the grind for bigger numbers, the main quest boils down to fighting 4 identical bosses, visiting a certain area after each fight, and not picking obviously suicidal dialog options when talking to the NPC in that area: the longest part is then getting to those 4 boss fights, as the late ones tend to be spawned so far out you'll be looking at several minutes of flying towards an objective marker.
    [*]If you for some reason want to grind for high level equipment the best way is to invest into Piloting, find a good vehicle spawn, and hunt Surveyors high in the sky as they can be bursted down quickly and have absurdly high level drops.
[/list]
